Take the sum as $\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} f(i)$.
For any real $t$: $t-1<[t]\le t$, so $\frac{k^2}{3^x}-1<\left[\frac{k^2}{3^x}\right]\le\frac{k^2}{3^x}$.
Add over $k=1$ to $n$ and divide by $n^3$: $\frac{1}{3^x}\cdot\frac{\sum k^2}{n^3}-\frac{1}{n^2}<\frac{1}{n^3}\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left[\frac{k^2}{3^x}\right]\le\frac{1}{3^x}\cdot\frac{\sum k^2}{n^3}$.
Since $\sum_{k=1}^{n} k^2=\frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}$, we get $\frac{\sum k^2}{n^3}\to\frac13$; also $\frac{1}{n^2}\to 0$.
By the squeeze theorem, $f(x)=\frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{3^x}=\frac{1}{3^{x+1}}$.
Then $\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} f(i)=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{3^{i+1}}=\frac{1/9}{1-1/3}=\frac{1}{6}$.
So $12\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} f(i)=12\cdot\frac16=2$.
Answer: 2
